newsitem.title: UK: Metals Outlook - Zinc poised to surmount $1,300.
newsitem.headline: Metals Outlook - Zinc poised to surmount $1,300.

text.p: Zinc prices, which repeatedly notched up fresh 4-1/2 year highs last week, are expected to move above the psychological $1,300 a tonne level this week.
The base metals complex should see some activity and excitement elsewhere too on Monday, with "third Wednesday" pricing taking place during the morning rings.
The market was edgy on Monday morning over an official denial from China of reports that it had suspended copper imports.
"The markets are a bit nervous about this. You never know with the Chinese, sometimes they say the opposite of what they mean," a market analyst said.
The markets might otherwise trade fairly routinely, unless there was a significant movement out of present ranges, notably in copper, currently furrowing between $2,330 and $2,375.
Zinc peaked at $1,292 on Friday, before ending at $1,290, with the market underpinned by falling stocks and by speculative interest.
"It's a good close and should continue up to $1,300," said Martin Squires, analyst at LME trader Rudolf Wolff and Co.
"The uptrend is re-accelerating...opening the way for the rise to extend to $1,300 at least. On a longer-term basis $1,400 could be the aim," analysts Investment Research of Cambridge said.
In the copper market a widening backwardation on Friday helped prices move away from the lower end of the week's range, with three months ending at $2,356.
"It's looking good again, it's starting to turn around. We may see it head back to test the $2,375 resistance," Squires said.
If copper could resume upward momentum it should stiffen the sinews of the aluminium market, which closed last week at $1,668.
Prices have been faltering recently at tough overhead resistance, although the market has been helped by steady physical premiums.

"The uptrend is slowing distinctly now as psychological resistance at $1,700 is faced. However, there is a chance it could be resumed whilst support immediately below $1,640 holds," Investment Research added.
On Monday, LME members will be voting at an extraordinary general meeting to alter the market's Articles of Association, which will increase Board numbers by two.

The proposal, which follows the Securities and Investment Board review of the metal market last December, is intended to change the balance on the LME Board. With two further invited directors, the eight ring-dealing members can in theory be out-voted by the non-ring dealing/invited constituents.
